content:
Apple Cash's terms and conditions have just been updated, and Apple is notifying users of two upcoming changes.

Apple Cash will begin requiring users to verify their identity to add funds to their balance, and may enable an "externally initiated funds transaction" feature.

If you use Apple Cash, you may have just received an email, or will soon receive one, notifying you of changes to the service's terms and conditions.

Apple partners with Green Dot Bank to offer Apple Cash, and the bank's revised terms page (available here) contains several important changes that Apple specifically mentions in the email.

The first relates to identity verification. According to Apple:

Another upcoming change involves "externally initiated funds transactions." Although no firm date has been set, the new terms give Green Dot the ability to offer the feature. Apple writes:

The only other change Apple highlights in the email involves the arbitration section of Green Dot's terms. Aside from Apple encouraging users to review the changes carefully, no specific updates are mentioned, as the changes relate to users' rights and the procedures for handling disputes.

Did you find any other changes in the revised Apple Cash terms? Let us know in the comments.
